baslik: Motoseyir — The motorcyclist’s sat nav for twisty roads
aciklama: Motoseyir is a motorcycle sat nav that plans by distance, not by minutes. Back roads, coast and enduro modes, a tour generator, 1,600+ mountain passes, group rides and CarPlay.
og_baslik: Motoseyir — The motorcyclist’s sat nav for twisty roads
og_aciklama: Distance-first routing, back roads, a tour generator, 1,600+ mountain passes, group rides, intercom and CarPlay — in one app.
jsonld_aciklama: Distance-first navigation app for motorcyclists: shortest route, back roads, tour generator, mountain passes, group riding, intercom, CarPlay and legendary routes.
jsonld_ucretsiz: Unlimited routing and navigation in Türkiye, Europe and the USA, 1 saved tour; Pro’s 3-month and yearly plans include a 7-day free trial outside Türkiye, for new subscribers.
jsonld_pro: AI CoRider, CarPlay, group creation and intercom, Discover, tour generator, unlimited tours and trails, Back roads and Coast modes and best order for multiple stops.
hero_alt: A motorcyclist riding a twisty mountain road along the coast in the light of sunset
hero_lead: Motoseyir plans by distance, not by minutes. Back roads, coast or enduro, you choose. Or tell it which way you want to ride and let it build the tour; or pick a mountain pass and go.
hero_micro: Routing and navigation are free and unlimited in Türkiye, Europe and the USA; no account needed.
s2_t: legendary roads of Türkiye, Europe and the USA, ready as routes
s3_t: your route on the car screen, full screen
s4_t: same route, talking as you ride
k1_alt: Navigation screen in Motoseyir: next turn, distance left and speed
k1_p: It compares the alternatives between the same two points and suggests the shortest. On a multi-stop tour it works out the order of the stops, too. The rest is up to you.
k1_a_d: The default; it goes by kilometres.
k1_b_d: Leaves the main road for the twisty ones.
k1_c_d: Looks for gravel and unpaved roads.
k2_alt: Tour generator screen: direction and duration dial
k2_h2: Pick a direction and a time, the tour is ready.
k2_p: Turn the dial to the way you want to go and choose how many hours you have. Motoseyir draws a tour in that direction; you see it on the map and start if you like it.
k3_alt: Mountain passes screen: a map of Alpine passes with an altitude list
k3_p: Every pass has its altitude and exact location, and most have photos. Passes that close in winter show the months they’re closed, and dirt roads are marked as dirt. Add the ones you like to your tour and go.
k4_alt: AI CoRider screen: planner and chat options
k4_p: AI CoRider is a riding partner that talks to you through your helmet. Press the button and ask: it knows your route, searches along it, adds stops and changes the route for you. You hear the answer in your helmet and your hands stay on the bars.
k5_alt1: Group ride screen: the route on the map and the next turn
k5_alt2: Motoseyir navigation on a CarPlay screen
k5_h2: Ride as a group, talking as you go.
k5_p: Take the same route as your friends and see everyone on the map. Joining a group by invite or code is free.
k5_a_d: Meeting point, live location, one route.
k5_b_d: Talk to the group while you ride; no extra hardware.
k5_c_d: Your route on the car screen; the phone stays in your pocket.
k6_alt: Discover screen: stops along the route and their list
k6_p: See the back roads, beach roads, campsites and places to eat along your route, and add the ones you like.
k7_alt: A sample from a trip map video: the Istanbul–Athens route
k7_h2: The road you rode stays with you.
k7_p: Record the ride, watch it again later, and turn it into a trip map video to share.
k7_a_d: Watch the way you rode again on the map.
k7_b_d: Turn your tour into a short video.
k7_c_d: If rain is forecast at your stops, you see it on the route.
k7_d_d: Bring the route you already have into the app.
k8_alt: The motorcycle that stands for you on the map; drag left or right to turn it
k8_p: While you ride, a marker stands for you on the map. You pick it from the grid in Settings: bike, chopper, maxi scooter, touring, arrow or helmet.
k9_alt: Legendary roads screen: a list of ready-made routes and their map
k9_p: The famous roads of Türkiye, Europe and the USA come as ready-made routes: Tail of the Dragon, Beartooth Highway, Big Sur and more. Pick one and go.
k10_p: What’s inside the app, in two minutes.
fiyat_h2: Free to ride, Pro when you want more.
plan_u_p: Route planning and turn-by-turn navigation are unlimited in Türkiye, Europe and the USA. No account needed; the free tier keeps 1 saved tour.
plan_p_p: The 3-month and yearly plans start with a 7-day free trial outside Türkiye, for new subscribers. Pro unlocks:
pp6: Back roads and Coast modes, best order for multiple stops
fiyat_not: Current prices vary by region; you see them on the subscription screen in the App Store. Cancel anytime in your App Store account.
y118_1: Fixed a crash when switching from Blog to Feed in Community.
y118_2: Recording a video of your 3D ride replay starts more reliably.
y118_3: “Ready” no longer shows before the map has loaded, and the camera no longer jumps when you finish a pinch zoom.
y117_1: Trip map: watch a long tour or ride as a video on a clean map. As your route draws itself, the towns you passed and your photos appear one by one.
y117_2: New shortcuts on the Start screen: home and work, record a ride, a one-hour loop from here, a legendary road nearby.
y117_3: 298 mountain passes and six new legendary roads in the USA, and Coastal mode now works across Europe too.
y117_4: “Get to know Motoseyir” in Settings is a short video tour of the app, tab by tab.
y116_1: Watch in 3D: replay a recorded ride as if you were following from a helicopter; your photos pop up where you took them.
y116_2: Share as video: make a 15, 30 or 60-second vertical video, ready for Instagram. No Pro needed.
y116_3: Ride analysis: moving time, real breaks, sharp curves, total climb, and how much of the road was new to you.
y116_4: In Tour Generator, “Another one” brings three new loops on different roads, and you can avoid highways, tolls and dirt roads.
v_yuksek_h: The five highest in the US, all in Colorado
v_n1_d: The OpenStreetMap point that marks the pass. It sits on the road at the summit, not at an encyclopedia’s rough coordinate.
v_n2_d: From the pass’s Wikipedia or Wikidata entry, or OpenStreetMap when there isn’t one. It’s the road’s highest point.
v_n3_d: From the road’s seasonal closure tag in OpenStreetMap. If your tour crosses a pass that may be closed that month, the app tells you.
v_n4_d: Passes you ride over are ticked off from your ride log automatically. No internet needed.
v_atif: Location and closure data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Photos from Wikimedia Commons; each one shows its author and licence in the app.
a1_s1_t: free navigation in Türkiye, Europe and the US
a1_s3_t: alternative routes, with the shortest marked
a1_1_d: Before a junction it shows which lane to be in, on the phone and on CarPlay, and says it out loud.
a1_2_d: Where the limit is known, the speed sign stays on screen.
a1_3_d: Knows all 726 cameras in Türkiye from OpenStreetMap and warns you once per camera, 500 m or 20 seconds before it.
a1_4_d: Uses your phone’s best voice in your language. Switch to short prompts if you’d rather hear less.
a1_5_d: One tap takes toll roads out of the route.
a1_6_d: Your next turn shows on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island, so you don’t have to unlock the phone.
a2_s1_t: tour length, or pick it in hours
a2_s2_t: curve levels: Relaxed, Twisty, Very twisty
a2_1_d: Turn the dial or choose “Any direction”. The tour brings you back to where you started.
a2_2_d: Tell it how long you have, in half-hour steps, and Motoseyir turns that into distance.
a2_3_d: Switch off motorways, tolls and dirt roads, each on its own.
a2_4_d: You get the three best options. Don’t like them? “Another one” finds new ones on different roads.
a2_5_d: Each tour lists the mountain passes it goes over.
a2_6_d: Anyone can generate a tour and see it on the map. Saving twisty or motorway-free tours is part of Pro.
a4_s3_t: minute add-on packs that never expire
a4_1_d: Adds, removes and skips stops. Changes your destination and puts stops in order.
a4_2_d: Looks for fuel, food or a place to stay up the road and mentions the best-rated first.
a4_3_d: Ask about the weather, rain on your route and how far your tank will take you. For range, enter once in Settings how far you ride on a full tank.
a4_4_d: Tells you where everyone is and sends the group a ready-made alert for you: falling behind, break, hazard or fuel.
a4_5_d: Starts or ends navigation, turns on ride recording and takes you home.
a4_6_d: Pro renews 10 minutes of talk time every 30 days, and the free trial includes 5. If you need more, add a 30, 60 or 180 minute pack that never expires.
a5_s2_t: to join with a code or an invite
a5_s3_t: categories to search along the route on CarPlay
a5_1_d: Type the 8-character code or tap the link. Creating a group is part of Pro.
a5_2_d: Your location is shared only while navigation is running, and sharing stops when you end it.
a5_3_d: No push-to-talk on the intercom: just talk. Mute anyone you like. Nothing is recorded.
a5_4_d: Invite CoRider into the group’s room and everyone hears it.
a5_5_d: Map, turns and lanes on the car screen. Skip a stop, record the ride or answer an intercom call from there.
a5_6_d: In CarPlay Dashboard your next turn sits next to your other apps.
a6_s2_t: camping and nature spots in Türkiye
a6_1_d: All, Bay & beach, Camping & nature, Food & drink, Fuel and Passes.
a6_2_d: Shows how far ahead a place is, how far off the route, and which side of the road it’s on.
a6_3_d: Move the map anywhere and search around that spot.
a6_4_d: Campsites, RV parks, national parks, waterfalls, caves, lakes, picnic areas and hiking trails.
a6_5_d: From Wikimedia Commons. On iPhone, tapping a place also opens Apple’s place card.
a6_6_d: Passes and legendary roads are ranked by how well known they are.
a7_1_d: Moving time and real stops, sharp bends per 100 km, total climb, 10 km sections. All worked out on your phone.
a7_2_d: See what share of the ride was on roads you’d never ridden before.
a7_3_d: Replay the ride on Apple’s 3D satellite map at 1, 5, 20 or 60 times speed.
a7_4_d: First ride, total distance, 500 km in one ride, sunrise and night rides, weekly streaks, climbing, Everest height, pass collecting, three countries.
a7_5_d: Export rides as timestamped GPX files, and bring in a GPX route you already have.
a7_6_d: Send the video to your Instagram Story or get a share link for the ride.
a9_1_d: Stelvio, Grossglockner, Transfăgărășan, Trollstigen, the Atlantic Road, Galibier and more.
a9_2_d: Tail of the Dragon, Beartooth, Going-to-the-Sun Road, Big Sur, the Million Dollar Highway and more.
a9_3_d: Şile–Ağva, the Lycian coast on the D400, Assos and Mount Ida, the Datça peninsula, the Ayder highlands and more.
a9_4_d: European and US roads come with sources, summit height, and the number of bends and hairpins.
a9_5_d: Which months it’s open and whether it closes in winter, so you can check before you go.
a9_6_d: Pick a road and the route is ready to ride.
c_say_p: These are examples. There are no commands to memorise; say it in your own words.
c_s1: How far to go? Is it going to rain on the way?
c_s2: Any good place to eat on the way?
c_t2: Searches along your route, best-rated first
c_s3: Add the first one as a stop.
c_t3: Adds the stop and updates the route
c_s5: Will my fuel get me there?
c_t6: Looks for a place to stay
c_s7: Tell the group we’re stopping for a break.
c_t7: Sends the group a ready-made alert
c_s8: Remind me to oil the chain tomorrow.
c_t8: Saves the note and tells you the next day
c_h1_d: Tap the AI CoRider button on the map and start talking.
c_h2_d: No commands to learn. It answers in the language you speak.
c_h3_d: If your helmet is connected to the phone over Bluetooth, the voice comes through it. Can’t hear it in the wind? Just say “turn it up”.
c_vid_p: A real recording from the app: the rider asks how far is left and whether it will rain, asks for a place to stop, and the one they pick goes into the route as a stop.
c_vid_not: Real screen recording from the app.
c_vid_alt: AI CoRider by voice: the rider asks about time left and rain, finds a place to stop and adds it to the route
c_gz_p: Privacy. AI CoRider only runs when you turn it on. We don’t record or store your voice; what you say goes to a third-party cloud voice service so it can answer. Your raw location doesn’t go to that service; from your route it only gets text such as the distance left and the next manoeuvre. The session closes when you end it, after a while without speech, or when navigation ends.
c_gz_l: Details are in the privacy policy.
a4_7_d: “Planner” knows your route and gets things done; it comes with Pro. In “Chat” you pick the topic and it remembers earlier conversations; it opens with a minute pack.
a4_8_d: Call AI CoRider into the group intercom and everyone in the room hears it. The minutes come from the account of whoever called it.
a4_9_d: Keeps the notes you ask for and forgets them when you say “forget that”. Finds someone in your contacts; one tap on the screen places the call.
